contractCases.expected: All exported Sidebar parts are preserved. SidebarProvider defaults defaultOpen=true and supplies desktop open/state, openMobile, isMobile, setOpen/setOpenMobile and toggleSidebar through useSidebar; Sidebar itself accepts side left|right, variant sidebar|floating|inset and collapsible offcanvas|icon|none. Desktop widths are16rem, icon3rem, mobile18rem. The pinned use-mobile hook is false during SSR/initial render and tracks window.innerWidth<768 using matchMedia afterward. Desktop openProp and onOpenChange should be supplied as a pair: setOpen calls the handler instead of internal state whenever a handler exists, even without an openProp. The callback is boolean-only, not cancellable eventDetails. Every desktop setOpen request writes sidebar_state=true|false, path=/, max-age604800; the provider does not read that cookie automatically, and a rejected/ignored controlled request can still write its candidate. Mobile toggle only changes openMobile, with no desktop onOpenChange or cookie write. The two states are not synchronized/reset on breakpoint changes. collapsible=none bypasses responsive Sheet/collapse rendering even though provider state can still change. Trigger calls caller onClick then always toggles (defaultPrevented is not a veto); Rail is native button tabindex=-1 and needs explicit type=button in a form-safe reference. Provider always registers lowercase Ctrl/Meta+b globally while mounted, including editable targets; there is no disable-shortcut prop, so this reference uses one provider and documents that application constraint. SidebarInset is main; avoid nested main landmarks. Header/Footer/Group/Content are containers, Menu/Sub are native lists, and MenuButton defaults button via useRender: actual navigation deliberately renders anchors. isActive only supplies appearance/data-active, not aria-current; caller supplies current-page semantics. GroupLabel requires caller heading choice. Skeleton has random50–89% width and no loading announcement; use the completed Skeleton usage policy. Optional tooltip is visual-only and shown collapsed desktop, so native names remain complete. Mobile Sidebar composes Sheet with fixed title Sidebar/description Displays the mobile sidebar and hides its direct default Close button in source CSS; this reference supplies an explicit nested Close navigation control. Desktop icon collapse is chosen to keep intended navigation available; offcanvas CSS alone does not supply an inert/focus-removal guarantee.

Native Trigger Enter/Space and registered Ctrl/Meta+b toggle the appropriate viewport state. Desktop collapse does not become a dialog or trap focus. Mobile uses the real Sheet/Dialog focus, Escape and restoration policy; its trigger aria-expanded uses openMobile, not the desktop state. Navigation links retain native Tab/Enter and readable names when icon-collapsed. Rail is an optional pointer duplicate, not the sole keyboard access. Names, landmark label, heading and active-page relation are explicit caller composition.
